brief.headline: Continuity Guardian could not produce a grounded review
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 116922 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 28% over 30s (87/120 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $13,340/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, pid 116922) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $13,340/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: pid 116922 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_inventory, idle in transaction, txn open 4.0s) is the root blocker holding locks that cause 12 sessions to wait and checkout timeouts [DB-1]. Checkout success is 55% over 15s with 27 timeouts [TEL-1], and business impact shows 77% success vs 95% SLO with $4,155/min at risk [BIZ-1]. Waiting costs ~$199,211 and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance [BIZ-5]. The workload is replayable=True, policy may_interrupt, replay cost 4 min, typical runtime 900s [BIZ-3]. No protected settlements are in flight [DB-2]. No active change-calendar window covers batch_replayable_inventory [BIZ-2]. MEM-1 records a verified pact where terminating batch_replayable_inventory restored checkout to 100% over 10s [MEM-1].

audit.report: A replayable inventory reconciliation batch job (pid 116922) held an open transaction for 4.0 seconds and blocked 12 sessions, degrading checkout. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker because checkout success fell to 55% over 15 seconds with 27 timeouts, versus a 95% SLO, putting about $4,155 per minute at risk. Evidence showed waiting would cost roughly $199,211 and exceed the business's 60-second degradation tolerance, while termination meant a 4-minute replay of an idempotent job. The Continuity Guardian failed to produce a grounded review twice, so the negotiation escalated to inventory-platform without executing any action. Checkout remained degraded and the business was not recovered by the end of the trace.
audit.root_cause: The batch_replayable_inventory job held an open transaction that blocked checkout sessions, and no guardian action was executed because the Continuity Guardian could not ground its review.
lessons: For batch_replayable_inventory, pre-approve termination of idle-in-transaction blockers during checkout hours since the job is idempotent, replayable, and costs only 4 minutes to replay.
Monitor open-transaction duration for inventory_reconcile and alert before it blocks 12 sessions and drives checkout success below the 95% SLO.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian built a complete, evidence-backed case in one round, while the Continuity Guardian wasted the only round by failing grounding twice and never offering an alternative or confirming the business impact.
follow_ups: Ask inventory-platform to confirm whether pid 116922 was terminated and whether inventory_reconcile resumed from its checkpoint.
Add a runbook step for the Continuity Guardian to ground reviews using DB-1, TEL-1, BIZ-1, and BIZ-5 before escalation.
Review why the Continuity Guardian failed grounding twice and update its evidence checklist for batch workloads.
